newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Treasury plans interest rate swaps.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Treasury plans interest rate swaps.

text.p: The Australian Treasury said on Wednesday it planned to utilise domestic interest rate swaps in the 1997/98 financial year in a programme probably totalling between A$2.0 billion and A$3.0 billion.

Speaking to a financial markets conference Tony Hinton, first assistant secretary of the Treasury's investment and debt division, said swaps were needed because the government's reduced debt issuance program would otherwise make it difficult to meet both market risk and funding risk objectives.

"On current indications for 1997/98 it would not be possible to both maintain liquidity across the curve and achieve domestic portfolio duration objectives in line with the benchmark target," said Hinton.
"It is a classic instance of too few instruments chasing too many objectives," he said.

The duration target is around 3-1/4 years for the domestic portfolio, the composition of which is intended to minimise the cost of Commonwealth debt over the long term, subject to an acceptable degree of volatility in annual debt service costs, he said.

Hinton said it was too early to say precisely what size of programme was needed, but as 1997/98 bond issuance was likely to be weighted toward the longer-dated stocks, it was sensible to anticipate a reasonably sizeable program.
"For the purposes of a very broad indication, I note that a programme perhaps in the order of A$2.0 billion to A$3.0 billion might be anticipated," said Hinton.
Hinton emphasised that any swaps undertaken would be executed solely for portfolio management purposes, specifically to maintain domestic portfolio duration in line with the benchmark.
"Any such transactions should not be read in any way, shape or form as signalling a Treasury view on the direction of interest rates," said Hinton.
Treasury would have a rigorous and prudent system for managing the counterparty credit risk exposures inherent in the swaps program, he added.

The Australian Financial Markets Association defines an Australian dollar interest rate swap as transactions in which payments determined by reference to a fixed rate of interest are exchanged for payments determined by reference to bank bill-rates, which are floating. --Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
